Team — thanks again for covering the interview loop yesterday. Short ask: please upload your scorecards and any short bullets on risks/strengths to the Drive folder linked below by EOD Tuesday so we can decide whether to move Sofia to final onsite.

Quick guidance for the note (1–3 bullets each):
- Top 1 strength (skill or behavioral)
- Top 1 concern / blocking question
- Hireability recommendation (yes/bench/no) + suggested next step (e.g., final onsite, take-home, decline)

Uploading my scorecard — attaching a filled PDF and a short screen clip of the design exercise. Highlights below.

Scorecard (attached: sofia_scorecard_marissa.pdf)
Recording stub: sofia_screen_recording.mp4

Bullets:
- Strength: Systems thinking + pragmatic tradeoffs — designed a caching strategy that balanced memory and latency effectively during the whiteboard.
- Concern: Limited prior infra ownership; answers on long-term operational tradeoffs were high-level, not concrete.
- Recommendation: bench -> final onsite only if we pair with a strong infra-focused hire on panel; otherwise move to take-home deep-dive on scalability design.

If helpful, I can flag a couple of final onsite questions that probe operational ownership.

—Marissa

Quick note from my side (I left a short comment in the Drive doc):
- Strength: Communication + product sense — connected tradeoffs to customer impact well.
- Concern: Confidence gap on low-level debugging; gave plausible high-level paths but deferred specifics multiple times.
- Recommendation: +1 for final onsite on culture/PM cross-functional fit; neutral on IC technical ownership. Suggest a focused debugging exercise or a short take-home bug-hunt.

Adding my notes; copied below and uploaded a one-pager to the Drive folder.

- Strength: Readable code and test-first mindset; implemented the sample endpoint with clear tests during pairing.
- Concern: Operational edge-cases were missed — specifically error handling for partial KV-cache misses and recovery strategy. I asked a follow-up and got reasonable direction but no concrete rollback pattern.
- Recommendation: move to take-home deep-dive (6–8 hour) focused on resilience and observability. If she nails that, invite to final onsite.

Grace — synthesizing what's here: majority recommend a focused take-home to validate infra ownership. If we agree, next steps for Amit: (1) confirm candidate availability for take-home next week, (2) deliver take-home instructions + rubric, (3) we review in 72 hours.

Amit — can you confirm Sofia's availability? If yes, I'll send the take-home doc + rubric and lock reviewers (Marissa + Jonas + Kimberly).

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Principal Software Engineer
Redwood Inference
